takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — work customers have signed for but Oracle has not yet delivered — jumped 44% to $98B. Oracle said it signed the largest sales contracts in its history in Q3 and Q4, including over 30 AI contracts worth more than $12.5B in Q4 alone, one of them with OpenAI to train ChatGPT in the Oracle Cloud.
takeaways.title: The backlog surged 44%

takeaways.text: Cloud revenue — infrastructure plus applications — rose 20% to $5.3B, with cloud infrastructure alone up 42% to $2.0B and cloud applications up 10% to $3.3B. That growth more than covered a 15% drop in new license sales and declines in hardware and services.
takeaways.title: Cloud is carrying the growth

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 13% to $4.7B, but net income still fell 5% to $3.1B: Oracle paid $878M of interest in the quarter, and the tax line swung from a $210M benefit a year ago to a $639M charge this time.
takeaways.title: Debt and tax ate the operating gain

verdict: Oracle's revenue rose 3% to $14.3B and it kept $3.1B as profit — but the real story was its backlog of signed contracts, which surged 44% to $98B as customers booked AI cloud capacity.
